global_caption: The video contains 11 shots. It is a warm-toned, realistic-style home gardening tutorial filmed beside a transparent balcony plant stand, primarily lit by natural daylight with soft backlighting. The camera movement is steady and delicate, featuring continuous gentle Chinese The emotional tone remains uniformly warm, calm, and approachable.
shot1: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide eye-level composition. The plant stand and table form horizontal leading lines. In the foreground are neatly arranged pots, perlite, potting soil, and seedlings; in the background, sunlight illuminates railings and greenery. Moderate depth of field keeps tools and environment clearly visible. A middle-aged woman stands slightly off-frame, gently holding a pot, gesturing while softly introducing in Chinese that today’s task is transplanting seedlings. The camera slowly pushes in slightly. Bird calls and wind establish the balcony atmosphere first.
shot2: Shot 2 hard-cut transition from previous shot. Close-up overhead view focused on bottom of pot. Composition centers on drainage hole. Hands lift pot slightly and rotate it, fingers lightly tapping hole to confirm it's clear. Texture of clay pot and hole edges clearly visible. Natural light from behind and side creates soft contrast. Camera remains stable with micro-distance feel, no unnecessary shake.
shot3: Shot 3 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium close-up overhead view shifts to tabletop work area. Pot temporarily set aside. Potting soil and slow-release fertilizer placed centrally. Foreground features mixing spoon; background blurred foliage. Hands evenly sprinkle fertilizer into soil and mix thoroughly. Soil particles transition from layered to uniformly blended during stirring. Warm natural light enhances texture. Camera slightly lowers from above and stabilizes, emphasizing procedural precision.
shot4: Shot 4 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium close-up eye-level slightly overhead view of inner pot wall. Inner circular edge acts as natural frame. Focus on perlite falling into bottom of pot. Hands place perlite in handfuls; particles collide and quickly form an even thin layer. Lighting remains soft and natural. She explains “底部先铺一层陶粒，帮助排水”, with crisp Camera slightly pushes in, highlighting thickness change.
shot5: Shot 5 cuts abruptly from the previous shot, transitioning from a close-up high-angle view to a slightly perspective-enhanced medium close-up. Two hands slowly pour the mixed soil into the pot, gradually raising the soil level to about two-thirds of the pot's height. The soil edges naturally mound up and are gently smoothed by the palms. shot6: Shot 6 hard-cut from previous shot. Close-up overhead view locked on center of pot. Shallow depth of field focuses only on fingers, seedling root ball, and soil surface. Hands first dig a properly sized hole in center, then carefully place seedling root ball into hole. Root ball edges snugly contact loose soil. Leaves slightly tremble indicating gentle handling. Sunlight creates fine highlights along leaf edges. She explains in Chinese “在中心挖穴，把幼苗放正”, with Camera makes minimal push-in, emphasizing accurate root-soil contact.
shot7: Shot 7 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium close-up eye-level shot enters from side of pot rim. Foreground shows refilled soil; background blurred balcony railing. Hands evenly refill around root ball, then gently press with fingertips to stabilize plant. Soil surface transitions from loose to flat and compact. Seedling posture shifts from slight wobble to upright stability. Camera performs horizontal pan, following hands circling pot edge.
shot8: Shot 8 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium close-up side angle. Watering can slowly tilts from top of frame. Thin stream flows along pot edge. Composition uses pot rim as circular guide. Focus shifts from spout to darkened, moistened soil surface. Soil color changes from light to dark as it absorbs water, with small areas showing tiny reflective seepage. She softly explains “第一次沿盆边缓慢浇透”. Watering Camera slightly follows spout movement.
shot9: Shot 9 cuts abruptly from the previous shot, transitioning to a window-side location that creates a logical spatial extension. A medium shot at eye level frames the character alongside a potted plant, with the window frame and plant stand forming leading lines into the depth of the scene. In the foreground is a potted plant just watered, while the background features bright but not overexposed outdoor light. The character gestures toward the soft incoming light and a well-ventilated area, indicating the intended placement environment. Natural daylight continues to dominate the lighting. The wind The camera performs a gentle lateral pan, shifting the viewer's focus from the plant to the window-side position.
shot10: Shot 10 cuts hard from the previous shot, returning to a close-up, eye-level slightly high-angle view of the top of the potted plant, with focus on the leaves and label area. Two hands use small scissors to trim off a yellowing leaf, then insert a small tag marked with a date into the soil near the edge. After removing the leaf, the plant's overall shape appears neater; the tag wobbles slightly before stabilizing. Side-backlighting enhances the visibility of leaf veins and the surface of the label paper. The camera first gently pushes in toward the leaves, then slightly tilts down to the label.
shot11: Shot 11 soft fade-out/fade-in transition from previous shot. Pulls out to wide eye-level shot to conclude. Completed potted plant returned to plant stand. Foreground shows finished pot and tidy table. Background features balcony plants illuminated by warm sunlight. Composition is stable and open. Seedling stands upright, soil surface smooth, date label clearly visible. Woman gently holds pot edge, then withdraws hands naturally, facing camera to summarize. This closing statement perfectly aligns with visual display of finished product. Camera slowly pulls back and stops, ending the tutorial in a quiet, bright, and clearly completed atmosphere.
